correctness.rationale: The construction is sound. For all nondistinguished agents, constant second-coordinate layers give disjoint copies of the target relation; for the distinguished agent, the levels \(t-c(x)\) give the same. Hence all five listed relation properties transfer. If two distinct lifted worlds were jointly related by every agent, a nondistinguished relation forces equal second coordinates and the distinguished relation forces equal colors; their projections would then form a conflict edge with equal colors, impossible. Projection satisfies forth immediately and back by choosing either the same second coordinate or the unique shifted coordinate. In the universal two-agent S5 target, every equivalence class of either lifted relation maps surjectively by back and therefore has at least \(m\) points; one class meets at least \(m\) distinct classes of the other relation, giving \(m^2\). The one-agent obstruction follows directly from back on any off-diagonal target edge. The actual verifier checks the construction, bounded-morphism conditions, and property preservation on many finite instances, but the proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The result improves a general finite construction from a fixed quadratic size to an instance-sensitive chromatic parameter, identifies when that compression is strict, proves the quadratic worst case remains genuine in S5, and cleanly isolates the one-agent boundary. This is a motivated structural refinement rather than a cosmetic rewrite.
residual_risks: The chromatic bound need not be globally optimal for every target.

final_claim: For every finite relational model with \(m\) worlds and at least two agents, if \(q\) is the chromatic number of the joint-accessibility conflict graph, there is a proper bounded-morphic cover with exactly \(mq\) worlds that preserves reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, seriality, and Euclideanness relationwise; the quadratic bound is sharp on the two-agent universal S5 target, while with one agent a proper surjective bounded-morphic cover exists exactly when the target is already proper.
limitations: The achieved size \(m\chi(G_N)\) is not claimed minimal for every individual target.
The quadratic lower bound assumes the two lifted relations are equivalence relations, matching the S5 setting.
